newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki tracks overseas bourses higher.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki tracks overseas bourses higher.

text.p: * Finnish shares closed higher on Friday tracking overseas bourses, with a positive tone conquering early jitters over Wall St's Thursday dip. Nokia bullish, forestries firm.
Shares closed fair trade broadly higher on Friday, helped by strength on overseas bourses and by further gains in Nokia as the market mastered its early jitters over Wall Street's Thursday dip.
The HEX index rose almost a percentage point, and was up 1.5 percent on the week.
Trading picked up after a cautious start. "The tone turned out to be rather positive," one broker said. But the New York rally cannot last forever, another said looking to next week.
Nokia gained 3.50 markka to close at 263.00, and the share accounted for one third of total bourse turnover.

The forestry sub-index posted even stronger gains than the all-share HEX, with UPM-Kymmene rising 1.10 markka to 90.60. Enso tacked on 0.30 to end at 35.70 markka, and Metsa-Serla added 0.10 to close at 30.40 markka.

Brokers said forestries were boosted by recent strength in U.S. paper stocks and by upbeat comments from the industry in a barometer of business confidence published Thursday by the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers.
"There's nothing in their economic fundamentals that could be boosting them," one broker said.
Shares in passenger ferry operator Silja Oy rose 2.00 markka to 36.00 in lively trade after the group on Thursday announced plans to improve its capital structure through a debt-for-equity swap.
But brokers were mixed on whether the financial restructuring made Silja a more attractive stock.
"It should in fact have the opposite effect by diluting the stock, but then again liquidity will improve," one broker said.
